key_insight: GeSe can appear highly ductile or brittle depending on loading direction, size, and stress path, so plasticity in inorganic semiconductors must be judged with much stricter, multi-condition criteria.
engineering_relevance: For flexible and curved-surface electronics, material selection must consider anisotropic deformation and test geometry because a single compression result can overstate real mechanical robustness.
method: Bending along the c-axis armchair direction
Micropillar compression: conventional vs eccentric loading
evidence_signal: The abstract compares multiple tests and reports ~23% compressive strain without fracture in one orientation, brittle cleavage in bending, brittle fragmentation in conventional micropillars, and shear-assisted sliding under eccentric micropillar loading.
watch_item: A favorable plastic response in one test condition does not guarantee intrinsic ductility; results can be dominated by orientation, defects, and loading-induced stress constraints.
paper_title: Identifying Plastic Inorganic Semiconductors Requires More Rigorous Criteria
